location_rule: Absolute root of the GitHub repository, OR root of the GitHub release archive (zip) if the repo itself isn't laid out that way. For this monorepo, a gemini-extension.json would have to live at the git repo ROOT (outside npm-package/) to satisfy this rule — none exists there today.
version_field: `version` (string) inside gemini-extension.json. Displayed in the CLI UI, but NOT authoritative for update detection on git-clone or GitHub-release installs (see update_detection).
update_detection: Three distinct mechanisms depending on install method: (1) GitHub Releases install — CLI queries the GitHub API for the latest release tag and IGNORES the manifest `version` field; (2) Git-clone install — CLI runs `git ls-remote` and compares the remote HEAD commit hash to local HEAD; (3) Local-directory install — CLI compares the `version` field in the source manifest to the installed one. Docs advise keeping gemini-extension.json's version in sync with the GitHub release tag anyway, 'to prevent confusion' in the UI, not because it drives detection for release/git installs.
url_field: Not a single fixed field for the gallery itself (no submission URL). Inside mcpServers entries, the docs page only enumerates command/args/cwd explicitly for the example, and states generally that 'all MCP server configuration options are supported except for trust' — i.e. a remote entry's url/httpUrl field is not itself fully documented on this reference page (UNVERIFIED exact field name for remote transport in gemini-extension.json's mcpServers; command/args/cwd for local stdio IS confirmed).
auth_mechanism: Extension-declared `settings` array: each entry has name/description/envVar/sensitive. Values are collected from the user (stored in a per-extension `.env` file, or in the OS keychain if `sensitive:true`) at USER or WORKSPACE scope. Those collected values are merged into a `customEnv` map and substituted via `${VAR}` / `$VAR` / `${VAR:-default}` tokens into the WHOLE extension config object (gated behind the `experimental.extensionConfig` settings flag) — see blocking question (a) below for the exact source-code trace.
validator_cmd: No hosted JSON Schema exists for gemini-extension.json (confirmed absence — extensive doc search found no $schema reference). A `gemini extensions validate` CLI subcommand is referenced in a third-party GitHub issue thread but was not independently confirmed against an official command-reference page in this research pass.
publish_mechanism: Fully automatic, decentralized: (1) repo must be PUBLIC, (2) add the GitHub topic `gemini-cli-extension` to the repo's About section, (3) place gemini-extension.json at the absolute repo root. Google's crawler indexes tagged repos daily; there is no submission form, PR, or review step. (Real-world caveat: community GitHub issues show repos meeting all three documented requirements sometimes failing to appear in the gallery for weeks — treat 'passes the daily crawl' as probabilistic, not guaranteed, per the actual bug reports found.)
resubmit_on_version_bump: NO manual resubmission step exists or is needed — the crawler re-reads the tagged repo continuously. Users who already installed the extension receive the new version through whichever of the three update_detection mechanisms applies to their install method.

location_rule: `mcp-publisher publish` reads `./server.json` from the CLI's current working directory by default (an explicit path can also be passed positionally). For novada-mcp the CLI must therefore be run from inside `npm-package/` (where server.json already lives, correctly co-located with package.json). CONFIRMED consistency: server.json's `name` ("io.github.NovadaLabs/novada-mcp") matches package.json's `mcpName` field exactly, satisfying the registry's cross-check rule ('The name property in server.json must match the mcpName property in package.json').
version_field: Top-level `version` in server.json. CONFIRMED currently "0.9.41" — matches npm-package/package.json (not stale).
update_detection: None — the registry does not poll or auto-detect anything. The publisher must manually re-run the publish flow for every release; registry consumers see only whatever versions have been explicitly published.
url_field: `remotes[].url` for a streamable-http remote entry. CONFIRMED current value: "https://mcp.novada.com/mcp", with `remotes[].headers[].name = "Authorization"` describing the Bearer-token convention (informational metadata shown to registry consumers, not an enforced auth check by the registry itself).
auth_mechanism: Two SEPARATE auth layers must not be conflated: (1) PUBLISHING auth (who may push to this name) — either GitHub OAuth device-flow (`mcp-publisher login github`, binds the name to `io.github.<user-or-org>/*`) or domain-ownership proof via DNS TXT record or an HTTP file at `/.well-known/mcp-registry-auth` (binds the name to `<reverse-dns-domain>.*`, used with a generated Ed25519/ECDSA key pair); (2) the SERVER's own runtime auth, which for novada-mcp's hosted remote is `Authorization: Bearer <NOVADA_API_KEY>`, declared only descriptively in server.json's `remotes[].headers`.
schema_url: https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json — CONFIRMED: this exact URL is both what the official quickstart generates via `mcp-publisher init` AND what is already present in novada-mcp's existing server.json ($schema field) — current, not stale.
validator_cmd: No dedicated `mcp-publisher validate` subcommand was found in the publisher CLI's documented command set (init/login/publish only, per the contributor README). JSON-syntax validity can be checked generically with `node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('server.json'))"`; full schema conformance is enforced server-side by the registry at publish time, not by a standalone local command.
publish_mechanism: One-time `mcp-publisher login <github|github-oidc|dns|http>` to authenticate, then `mcp-publisher publish` (reads ./server.json) for every release. There is explicitly NO merge-to-registry-repo-via-PR path: 'adding a server.json won't publish or list your server, even if merged' into the modelcontextprotocol/registry GitHub repo.
resubmit_on_version_bump: YES, CONFIRMED explicitly by the registry's own FAQ: 'How do I update my server metadata? Submit a new server.json with a unique version string. Once published, version metadata is immutable (similar to npm).' — every version bump requires a fresh `mcp-publisher publish` run with a new, never-before-used version string; there is no way to mutate an already-published version in place, and no delete/unpublish capability exists yet ('Currently, no' — open GitHub discussion).
